title: Sentence Similarity II
summary: Given two sentences represented as arrays of words and a list of similar word pairs, determine if the sentences are similar.
statement: Given two sentences represented as arrays of words and a list of similar word pairs, determine if the sentences are similar. Sentences are considered similar if they have the same number of words, and for each pair of corresponding words, they are similar. Note that a word is always similar to itself, and the similarity relation is transitive.
constraints: Words are similar to themselves, and supplied similarity pairs are symmetric and transitive.
Return whether every aligned word pair is similar.
hints: Model words as vertices joined by similarity pairs.
Union every supplied pair, then compare component representatives for aligned words.
Also accept identical aligned words directly.
Union-find computes exactly the symmetric transitive closure required by the definition.
editorial: Union-find computes exactly the symmetric transitive closure required by the definition.
